summary: The President's PhD Scholarships are funded by Imperial College London for 3.5-year PhD study at Imperial. For the 2027-28 entry cycle there are 50 scholarships, open to excellent candidates from the UK and worldwide with no nationality restriction. An award pays tuition fees, a stipend of GBP 27,036 a year (2027-28 rate) and a consumables fund, plus access to a programme of events for scholars. There is no separate scholarship form: candidates apply for PhD admission and choose the scholarship option.
eligibility_notes:
Open to applicants from Imperial, the UK and worldwide, with no nationality restrictions. Some departments may be unable to support international candidates. Only new PhD applications count; current Imperial PhD students are not eligible. Full-time and part-time study are both eligible.

Academic criteria: a first-class or equivalent result in an undergraduate or integrated master's degree (or one that is due), and a distinction in a standalone master's (or evidence of high performance that will lead to one). A candidate with only one undergraduate degree or integrated master's needs a first-class result even if they hold a master's. International candidates should check with the relevant Admissions team that their grades meet the criteria.

Special routes: a department may nominate a candidate who missed the criteria for extenuating reasons but shows the required calibre (contact the department before applying), and candidates with non-traditional academic or career paths and strong research potential are encouraged to apply under the 'alternate pathways' route.

A supervisor in an Imperial department must have agreed to supervise the candidate before applying, and a supervisor can supervise only one scholar at a time. A list of supervisors who are unavailable is published.

English language: the entry requirement for the PhD course applies. The central page lists IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 in each element (Standard) or 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in each (Higher), and other accepted tests (for example TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, Duolingo, LanguageCert, OET). The tier for a course is on its course page. Test scores are valid if taken within two years of the start date. Applicants need not hold the result when applying; it can be an offer condition. Doctoral students must also meet the College's Doctoral Academic Communication Requirement.
age_experience_notes: No age limit stated. Research experience is considered in the assessment of research potential.
funding_summary: Full funding for tuition fees, a stipend of GBP 27,036 per year (2027-28 rate) for living costs and a consumables fund of GBP 2,000 per year for the first three years, for a 3.5-year PhD. Scholars also get a programme of opportunities and events from the Early Career Researcher Institute and wider postgraduate support. The scholarship is for study with a start date between 1 August 2027 and 1 November 2027.
programmes_note: A research project of the candidate's choice with a supervisor at Imperial, in any of the four Faculties named by the page: Engineering, Medicine, Natural Sciences and Imperial Business School. The page does not list departments or topics; availability varies by department and some departments may not support international candidates. Candidates select the President's PhD Scholarship option in the funding section of the admission application and should check any extra requirements their department sets.
institutions_note: Imperial College London only. Each candidate applies to a department; the department nominates candidates and a College Selection Panel decides.

summary.detail: 3.5-year PhD at Imperial College London, full-time or part-time, starting between 1 August 2027 and 1 November 2027, in the Faculties of Engineering, Medicine, Natural Sciences and Imperial Business School. New PhD applications only.

requirements.text: Online PhD application through Imperial's doctoral admissions system (My Imperial). A candidate may apply for up to two courses in a year. Choose the President's PhD Scholarship option in the funding section of the additional questions tab. There is no separate scholarship form.

A two-page supporting document. Page 1: personal statement on motivation for Imperial and the scholarship and any other relevant information. Page 2: research proposal. Updated versions may be submitted if shortlisted. First person is encouraged.
Optional separate research proposal upload for a more detailed document, if the department requires it.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if the department requires it.

requirements.text: Two academic referees, such as a personal tutor or thesis supervisor. Do not name the proposed PhD supervisor.
Academic transcripts and degree results as part of the admission application; first-class or equivalent results (or due results) are needed.

Accepted English language test at the level set for the course (for example IELTS Academic 6.5 overall and 6.0 in each element at the Standard level), taken within two years of the start date. May be set as an offer condition.
requirements.conditional_rule: Unless exempt under Imperial's exemption rules.

requirements.text: Details of an agreed supervisor in an Imperial department, who must have agreed to supervise before the application; the supervisor must not be on the unavailable supervisors list.

application_steps.title: Find and agree a supervisor, and check eligibility
application_steps.detail: Choose a PhD course and department, contact a supervisor and get agreement to supervise before applying. Check that the supervisor is not on the unavailable list (each supervisor can have only one President's scholar at a time) and that your grades meet the criteria. Departments may have extra requirements; ask the department if you rely on the special-case or alternate pathways route.

application_steps.title: Submit the PhD admission application and select the scholarship
application_steps.detail: Apply through My Imperial with the two-page personal statement and research proposal, two academic referees (not the proposed supervisor) and transcripts. Select the President's PhD Scholarship option in the funding section. For 2027-28 entry the rounds close at 23:59 UK time on 2 November 2026 (round 1), 11 January 2027 (round 2) and 1 March 2027 (round 3). Start dates are from 1 August 2027 to 1 November 2027.

application_steps.title: Department shortlisting and interview
application_steps.detail: Your department nominates you on academic merit and research potential and shortlists eligible candidates for the College Selection Panel. Interviews are part of doctoral selection; the department statement reflects interview performance.

application_steps.title: Faculty ranking and College Selection Panel decision
application_steps.detail: Candidates are scored and ranked; Faculties make some initial offers, and the College Selection Panel (the Vice-Provost for Research, the Director of the Graduate School and the Faculty Vice-Deans for Research) makes final decisions, including offers from a ring-fenced allocation for alternate pathways candidates. Criteria: academic excellence (results, transcripts, class position, awards) and research potential (research experience, the research plan and the department statement). Candidates are told by 31 January 2027 (round 1), 15 April 2027 (round 2) or 31 May 2027 (round 3).

application_steps.title: Receive written confirmation and meet offer conditions
application_steps.detail: Successful candidates get written confirmation. Any PhD offer is conditional on achieving the predicted qualifications, and English language and the Doctoral Academic Communication Requirement still apply. Unsuccessful applicants are automatically considered for a standard PhD place.

application_steps.title: Start the PhD and join the scholar programme
application_steps.detail: Start between 1 August 2027 and 1 November 2027. Scholars take part in events and development courses from the Early Career Researcher Institute. Scholarship terms follow Imperial's scholarships and bursaries terms and conditions, and information for current scholars is on a login-only page that could not be read.
